slot.brief: Order a set of species like O2, O2+, O2−, O22− and NO+ by bond length/bond order using MO reasoning, combined with a resonance-bond-length comparison (e.g., carbonate C–O bonds) — tough multi-species ranking.

stem: Using MO bond orders to infer relative bond lengths, choose the increasing bond-length order for the listed diatomic species and the correct resonance description of $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$.
options: $\text{NO}^+<\text{O}_2<\text{O}_2^+<\text{O}_2^-<\text{O}_2^{2-}$; carbonate has three equal $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds of average bond order $\dfrac{4}{3}$
$\text{O}_2^{2-}<\text{O}_2^-<\text{O}_2<\text{O}_2^+<\text{NO}^+$; carbonate has three equal $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds of average bond order $\dfrac{4}{3}$
$\text{NO}^+<\text{O}_2^+<\text{O}_2<\text{O}_2^-<\text{O}_2^{2-}$; carbonate has one $\text{C}=\text{O}$ bond and two $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds
$\text{NO}^+<\text{O}_2^+<\text{O}_2<\text{O}_2^-<\text{O}_2^{2-}$; carbonate has three equal $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds of average bond order $\dfrac{4}{3}$

verdicts.working: Bond orders are NO⁺ = 3, O₂⁺ = 2.5, O₂ = 2, O₂⁻ = 1.5, and O₂²⁻ = 1, so bond length increases in the reverse order. Carbonate has three equivalent C–O bonds with average bond order 4/3 due to resonance.

working:
Bond orders: $\text{NO}^+=3$, $\text{O}_2^+=2.5$, $\text{O}_2=2$, $\text{O}_2^-=1.5$, $\text{O}_2^{2-}=1$; bond length increases as bond order decreases. In $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, average $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond order $=\dfrac{2+1+1}{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}$; resonance makes the three bonds equal.

Independent check: Bond orders are NO⁺ = 3, O₂⁺ = 2.5, O₂ = 2, O₂⁻ = 1.5, and O₂²⁻ = 1, so bond length increases in the reverse order. Carbonate has three equivalent C–O bonds with average bond order 4/3 due to resonance.
solution:
Bond length decreases as bond order increases. The bond orders are $3, 2.5, 2, 1.5, 1$ for $\text{NO}^+$, $\text{O}_2^+$, $\text{O}_2$, $\text{O}_2^-$, $\text{O}_2^{2-}$, respectively, giving the stated increasing bond-length order.
In $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, resonance makes the three $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds equivalent, with average bond order $
$$\dfrac{2+1+1}{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}$$
